```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(DBI)
library(duckdb)
library(dplyr)
library(dbplyr)
options(width = 90, dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)
dir.create("_demo", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## A science question, not a database project

**How did observed catch per unit effort change by year and stratum?**

- Start with a tow-level survey extract.
- Create a typed, reusable data snapshot.
- Query only what an analysis needs.
- Deliver a table and figure for a technical report or manuscript.
- Let a collaborator rerun the analysis without a database server.

::: notes
Suggested session: 45–60 minutes, including the exercise. Audience: intermediate
to advanced R users. The same pattern works for observer summaries, acoustic
observations, environmental covariates, and simulation ensembles, subject to
appropriate access controls.
:::

## What you will be able to do

1. Explain columnar storage, row groups, and selective reads.
2. Read and write Parquet using R and DuckDB.
3. Use SQL **or** dplyr without pulling the entire dataset into R.
4. Choose local files, GCS objects, or a database deliberately.
5. Publish traceable analysis inputs and outputs.

**Core demo:** runs locally after package installation.  
**Cloud snippets:** illustrative, not executed; require your approved environment.

## Keep three layers separate

| Layer | Examples | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| File format | CSV, Parquet | Encode data on disk |
| Query engine | DuckDB, PostgreSQL, Oracle | Execute queries |
| Storage / compute | Laptop, GCS / GCP VM | Hold bytes / run work |

**Parquet is not a database. DuckDB is not a cloud storage service.**

GCS is object storage in Google Cloud (GCP); it does not execute SQL.

# Why Parquet?

## CSV is a useful interchange format

But repeated analysis of large CSV extracts has costs:

- Parse text and infer types each time.
- Read through records even when using only a few columns.
- Resolve ambiguous dates, missing values, encodings, and identifiers.
- Reconstruct the same schema separately in each analysis.

Keep CSV for small handoffs and inspection. Do not equate “text” with
“self-documenting”: units and scientific meaning still need a data dictionary.

## Parquet: typed, compressed, column-oriented

- An open, binary format supported by many languages and engines.
- Stores a schema: numbers, strings, dates, nested structures, and nulls.
- Encodes and compresses similar values together within columns.
- Supports selective reads rather than always decoding the whole table.

**Typical benefit:** repeated analytical scans of a subset of columns.

**Not guaranteed:** smaller files or faster queries for every dataset.

::: {.source}
[Apache Parquet overview](https://parquet.apache.org/docs/overview/)
:::

## Inside one Parquet file

```text
survey.parquet
├── Row group 1: a horizontal batch of rows
│   ├── year column chunk       → compressed pages
│   ├── stratum column chunk    → compressed pages
│   └── catch_kg column chunk   → compressed pages
├── Row group 2: the next batch
│   └── the same column structure
└── Footer: schema, row-group locations, column statistics
```

Read `year` and `catch_kg`? Skip the other column chunks.  
Filter `year = 2024`? Statistics **may** let the reader skip row groups.

::: notes
Statistics such as minimum and maximum values can rule out a row group. They
cannot guarantee skipping if values overlap every group, statistics are absent,
or expressions cannot be pushed down. Sorting or clustering by frequent filter
columns can help. Not every reader uses every available Parquet optimization.
:::

## Three different kinds of skipping

| Optimization | What gets skipped? | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Projection pushdown | Unused columns | Select only catch and effort |
| Predicate pushdown | Row groups/pages where supported | Filter a date range |
| Partition pruning | Entire files/directories | `year=2024/` |

These are related, **not interchangeable**.

One tiny file will not demonstrate large-scale speedups. We will verify
correctness, not promise a benchmark.

## Choose formats by the work

| Format | Good fit | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|
| CSV | Small, broadly readable exchange | No enforced schema; parsing |
| RDS | R-specific objects and models | R-centric; not a selective tabular scan |
| Parquet | Shared analytical tables | Not row-by-row editing or a full R object |
| Database tables | Managed, mutable shared records | Server administration and access |

Parquet preserves supported data types, **not all R semantics**:
factor levels, custom attributes, units, and time-zone behavior need explicit checks.

## File layout matters on GCS

```text
gs://YOUR_BUCKET/survey/releases/v1/
  year=2022/part-000.parquet
  year=2023/part-000.parquet
  year=2024/part-000.parquet
```

- Hive-style partition names can expose `year` as a query column.
- Choose coarse partitions used by common filters; avoid one file per tow.
- Too many tiny objects add listing and request overhead.
- Start with moderately sized files; tune file/row-group sizes using real queries.

::: notes
Partitioning is a dataset layout convention, not a requirement of Parquet.
A Parquet file is immutable in normal use: updates generally rewrite files.
Do not treat directory listings as transactions or overwrite a published
snapshot while collaborators are reading it.
:::

# DuckDB: an analytical engine inside R

## No server required

- Embedded, in-process SQL engine; runs in your R session.
- Columnar, vectorized execution for scans, joins, and aggregations.
- Queries Parquet directly without importing it into a database first.
- Can use multiple CPU cores and spill many operations to local disk.
- Integrates with **DBI**, **dbplyr**, and the wider Arrow ecosystem.

Your laptop or VM does the work. “In-process” does not mean “unlimited memory.”

::: {.source}
[DuckDB introduction](https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/)
:::

## The example dataset

**Synthetic teaching data — not NMFS observations or an abundance index.**

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tow_id` | Unique teaching tow identifier |
| `year`, `tow_date` | Survey year and date |
| `stratum` | `shelf` or `slope` |
| `species` | Illustrative `pollock` label |
| `catch_kg` | Catch in kg; one missing value, one true zero |
| `effort_km2` | Swept area in km²; strictly positive |

24 tows, 2022–2024. Source: repository `data/survey.csv`, created for this deck.

## Read with an explicit schema

```{r}
#| label: load-survey
survey <- read.csv(
  "data/survey.csv", na.strings = "NA",
  colClasses = c("character", "integer", "character", "character",
                "character", "numeric", "numeric")
)
survey$tow_date <- as.Date(survey$tow_date)
stopifnot(
  nrow(survey) == 24L, !anyDuplicated(survey$tow_id),
  !anyNA(survey$effort_km2), all(survey$effort_km2 > 0),
  all(survey$catch_kg >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  sum(is.na(survey$catch_kg)) == 1L
)
knitr::kable(head(survey, 3))
```

::: notes
These checks encode assumptions about this particular teaching fixture. A
production validation step should also check allowed species/strata, date ranges,
join keys, units, confidentiality, and schema compatibility.
:::

## Connect and write a Parquet snapshot

```{r}
#| label: write-parquet
con <- dbConnect(duckdb(), dbdir = ":memory:")
duckdb_register(con, "survey_r", survey)
dbExecute(con, "
  COPY (SELECT * FROM survey_r ORDER BY year, stratum, tow_id)
  TO '_demo/survey.parquet' (FORMAT PARQUET, COMPRESSION ZSTD)
") |> invisible()
duckdb_unregister(con, "survey_r")
```

- Register an R data frame explicitly; no implicit global-object lookup.
- `:memory:` keeps database state ephemeral; the Parquet file persists.
- A file-backed connection, e.g. `dbdir = "_demo/analysis.duckdb"`, persists tables.
- Arrow alternative: `arrow::write_parquet(survey, "survey.parquet")`.

::: notes
Arrow is optional and is not required by the runnable deck. Writing a file
requires write permission. Re-rendering replaces only the named demo outputs.
In reusable functions, use on.exit(dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)) immediately
after connecting; this document closes the shared connection at the end.
:::

## Query the file, not an imported table

```{r}
#| label: parquet-view
dbExecute(con, "
  CREATE VIEW survey AS
  SELECT * FROM read_parquet('_demo/survey.parquet')
") |> invisible()
schema <- dbGetQuery(con, "DESCRIBE survey")
knitr::kable(schema[, c("column_name", "column_type", "null")])
```

The view stores a query, not another copy of the observations.

## SQL: aggregate before bringing data into R

```{r}
#| label: sql-summary
summary_sql <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT year, stratum,
         count(*) AS n_tows,
         count(catch_kg) AS n_observed,
         avg(catch_kg / effort_km2) AS mean_cpue
  FROM survey
  WHERE species = 'pollock'
  GROUP BY year, stratum
  ORDER BY year, stratum
")
```

`avg()` excludes nulls; `count(*)` does not. A zero catch remains a zero.

**Estimand:** unweighted mean of tow-level kg/km², not a ratio of sums.

## A report-ready result, with sample sizes

```{r}
#| label: summary-table
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(
  summary_sql, digits = 2,
  col.names = c("Year", "Stratum", "Tows", "Observed catch", "Mean kg/km²"),
  caption = "Synthetic survey: descriptive mean tow-level CPUE."
)
```

One missing catch reduces the 2023 slope sample size from four to three.
It is **not** silently converted to zero.

This is not a design-weighted abundance estimate. Real survey inference needs
sampling-design weights, uncertainty estimation, and domain review.

## The same query through dplyr

```{r}
#| label: dplyr-summary
lazy_summary <- tbl(con, "survey") |>
  filter(species == "pollock") |>
  group_by(year, stratum) |>
  summarise(
    n_tows = n(),
    n_observed = sum(as.integer(!is.na(catch_kg)), na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_cpue = mean(catch_kg / effort_km2, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(year, stratum)
summary_r <- collect(lazy_summary)
```

`tbl()` builds a lazy query; `collect()` retrieves the six-row result.
Not every R function translates to SQL: inspect before collecting.

## Inspect the SQL translation

```{r}
#| label: show-sql
show_query(lazy_summary)
```

Keep joins, filters, and summaries in DuckDB. Collect only the analysis-sized
result needed for a model, plot, or report.

## Make reproducibility executable

```{r}
#| label: validate-results
stopifnot(
  nrow(summary_sql) == 6L,
  all(as.numeric(summary_sql$n_tows) == 4),
  identical(as.numeric(summary_sql$n_observed), c(4, 4, 4, 3, 4, 4)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(summary_sql$mean_cpue,
                   c(20, 7, 22, 20 / 3, 24, 11))),
  isTRUE(all.equal(as.data.frame(summary_r), summary_sql,
                   check.attributes = FALSE))
)
cat("PASS: expected means, missingness, and SQL/dplyr agreement.\n")
```

The render fails if these checks fail. Agreement alone is insufficient:
compare against known answers and document the scientific assumptions.

## From query to manuscript figure

```{r}
#| label: fig-cpue
#| echo: false
#| fig-alt: "Synthetic mean CPUE rises from 20 to 24 kg per square kilometre on the shelf; slope values are 7, 6.67, and 11 in 2022 to 2024."
cpue <- xtabs(mean_cpue ~ year + stratum, data = summary_sql)
matplot(as.integer(rownames(cpue)), cpue, type = "b", pch = c(16, 17),
        lty = c(1, 2), col = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00"), xaxt = "n",
        xlab = "Year", ylab = expression("Mean tow CPUE (kg / km"^2*")"),
        ylim = c(0, 28))
axis(1, at = 2022:2024)
legend("topleft", legend = colnames(cpue), col = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00"),
       pch = c(16, 17), lty = c(1, 2), bty = "n")
```

Descriptive synthetic values only; no uncertainty intervals or population inference.
Retain zeros, report missingness, and justify the estimator before publication.

## Export the small result, retain provenance

```{r}
#| label: export-results
write.csv(summary_sql, "_demo/cpue-summary.csv", row.names = FALSE,
          na = "")
manifest <- data.frame(
  file = c("data/survey.csv", "_demo/survey.parquet"),
  md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(c("data/survey.csv", "_demo/survey.parquet")))
)
write.csv(manifest, "_demo/input-manifest.csv", row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), "_demo/session-info.txt")
```

Archive the source revision, query, input checksum, data dictionary, package
lockfile, and report together. MD5 here detects accidental changes, not tampering.

::: notes
For a real analysis, create and review a renv lockfile after choosing the team
environment. Pin the DuckDB package/engine as well as R packages. Byte-for-byte
Parquet files can differ across writer versions even when values agree, so
validate data content and schema as well as recording file checksums.
:::

## Inspect the plan before tuning

```{r}
#| label: explain-query
#| eval: false
dbGetQuery(con, "
  EXPLAIN ANALYZE
  SELECT avg(catch_kg / effort_km2)
  FROM read_parquet('_demo/survey.parquet')
  WHERE year = 2024
")
```

- `EXPLAIN`: planned operators. `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`: executes and measures.
- Check projected columns, filters, scanned rows, and elapsed time.
- Compare cold/warm runs on representative data, not this 24-row fixture.
- Record engine version, hardware, cache conditions, bytes read, and cost.

## Larger than R memory is not unlimited

```{r}
#| label: resource-settings
#| eval: false
dbExecute(con, "SET memory_limit = '4GB'")
dbExecute(con, "SET temp_directory = '/approved/local/scratch/duckdb'")
dbExecute(con, "SET threads = 4")
```

- Choose settings for the host; leave headroom for R and the operating system.
- Some allocations/operators exceed the buffer memory limit or cannot spill.
- Large joins/sorts need fast scratch space; avoid collecting raw observations.
- Check local disk capacity and protect sensitive temporary data.

# From a laptop to GCS / GCP

## Why Parquet works well over object storage

1. A reader fetches the footer to discover schema and byte ranges.
2. HTTP range requests fetch needed column chunks.
3. Statistics and partitions can reduce remote reads.

**Still costs something:** object listing, requests, network transfer, and compute.

- Use compute near the bucket: e.g. an approved GCP VM in the same region.
- Remote DuckDB queries run on that VM/laptop, **not inside GCS**.
- Broad scans, small files, and repeated cross-region reads can erase savings.

::: {.source}
[DuckDB Parquet tips](https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/data/parquet/tips)
:::

## GCS: public versus private access

```{r}
#| label: public-gcs
#| eval: false
dbExecute(con, "INSTALL httpfs")
dbExecute(con, "LOAD httpfs")
# Illustrative path: replace with an actual public Parquet object.
public_url <- "https://storage.googleapis.com/YOUR_PUBLIC_BUCKET/survey.parquet"
public_rows <- dbGetQuery(con, paste0(
  "SELECT count(*) AS n FROM read_parquet(",
  dbQuoteString(con, public_url), ")"
))
```

`httpfs` supports remote reads. Install extensions only from approved sources.
Public HTTPS needs no credentials; **never make restricted data public for a demo**.

## Private GCS: credentials are not interchangeable

DuckDB's documented `gs://` route uses GCS's S3-compatible API with **HMAC keys**.
These are not a service-account JSON file or a `gcloud` OAuth access token.

```{r}
#| label: private-gcs-secret
#| eval: false
# Supply approved GCS HMAC credentials outside this document.
stopifnot(nzchar(Sys.getenv("GCS_HMAC_KEY_ID")),
          nzchar(Sys.getenv("GCS_HMAC_SECRET")))
secret_sql <- paste0(
  "CREATE OR REPLACE SECRET gcs_read (TYPE gcs, KEY_ID ",
  dbQuoteString(con, Sys.getenv("GCS_HMAC_KEY_ID")), ", SECRET ",
  dbQuoteString(con, Sys.getenv("GCS_HMAC_SECRET")),
  ", SCOPE 'gs://YOUR_BUCKET/')"
)
invisible(dbExecute(con, secret_sql))
rm(secret_sql)
```

::: notes
Run the preceding httpfs installation/loading first. The default secret is
temporary, scoped to this database instance; do not use CREATE PERSISTENT SECRET
in a shared teaching environment. Never print the SQL string, enable query
logging around it, or put credentials in the deck, source control, or reports.
HMAC keys are long-lived secrets: use least-privilege bucket/object permissions,
approved secret delivery, and rotation. An organization may prohibit them;
consult your cloud/security team rather than bypassing policy.
:::

## Query a private release — without downloading it all

```{r}
#| label: private-gcs-query
#| eval: false
cloud_summary <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT year, stratum, avg(catch_kg / effort_km2) AS mean_cpue
  FROM read_parquet(
    'gs://YOUR_BUCKET/survey/releases/v1/year=*/*.parquet',
    hive_partitioning = true
  )
  WHERE year = 2024 AND species = 'pollock'
  GROUP BY year, stratum
  ORDER BY year, stratum
")
dbExecute(con, "DROP SECRET gcs_read")
```

If HMAC is not approved: stage an authorized, versioned subset using approved
Google tooling and query locally. A mounted bucket is not automatically a fast disk.

::: {.source}
[DuckDB GCS authentication and examples](https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/guides/network_cloud_storage/gcs_import)
:::

## A reproducible cloud release

- Write a **new release prefix**, validate, then publish its manifest.
- Record exact object names, GCS generation IDs, and checksums.
- Prefer immutable snapshots; enable retention/versioning per agency policy.
- Keep a schema, units, missing-value conventions, and release notes.
- Grant collaborators read-only access to the same approved objects.

**Important:** a wildcard over a changing prefix is not a frozen input.
An ordinary `gs://` query does not by itself pin object generations; use
immutable names or a verified, generation-pinned staging workflow.

## Which engine belongs where?

| Need | DuckDB | PostgreSQL / Oracle |
|---|---|---|
| One analyst scanning a snapshot | Excellent fit | Also possible; requires a service |
| Many users updating shared records | Not the usual fit | Designed for coordinated clients |
| Transactions and constraints | Supported locally | Centralized transactional systems |
| Per-user roles, auditing, service uptime | Not a server security boundary | Managed server controls |
| Portable analytical extract | File + R project | Export or database access |

In embedded mode, DuckDB supports concurrent work within a process; multiple
processes can read when none writes. Do **not** independently open one writable
`.duckdb` file from several R sessions or over a network drive.

::: notes
This comparison concerns the embedded R workflow, not all DuckDB deployments.
Newer versions also offer client-server access through the Quack protocol;
check current support and operational requirements before choosing it.
:::

::: {.source}
[DuckDB concurrency](https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/connect/concurrency)
:::

## DuckDB, BigQuery, or both?

- **DuckDB:** local/VM analysis, versioned Parquet, bounded compute, portable reports.
- **BigQuery:** managed distributed warehouse, shared SQL service, IAM and governance;
  storage/query or capacity costs depend on configuration.
- **PostgreSQL / Oracle:** authoritative shared records, transactional applications,
  controlled edits, organizational access and auditing.

**Common NMFS pattern:** authoritative database → approved versioned Parquet
extract on GCS → DuckDB in R → validated report/manuscript.

Large multi-user workloads may belong in the warehouse; benchmark and consult
data stewards rather than replacing an operational database.

## Collaboration is more than sharing a file

**In Git:** Quarto/R source, small public fixtures, schema, package lockfile,
queries, validation rules, and a release manifest.

**In approved data storage:** large snapshots, confidential inputs, and
access-controlled derived data. A Parquet file does not enforce row-level access.

**With the publication:** methods, estimator/weighting choices, exclusions,
data/code availability, software versions, and archived release identifiers.

Confirm confidentiality and disclosure review before publishing even summaries.
Preserve authoritative sources; avoid emailing divergent copies of “final.csv.”

## Exercise: produce a 2024 result

Using `tbl(con, "survey")`:

1. Filter to 2024 and `pollock`.
2. Compute tow-level `catch_kg / effort_km2`.
3. Summarize mean CPUE and observed sample size by stratum.
4. Collect **only** the summary.
5. Explain why averaging tow ratios differs from dividing total catch by total effort.

**Check your answer:** shelf = **24**, slope = **11** kg/km²;
four observed tows per stratum.

::: notes
Allow 5–10 minutes. Discuss the scientific target, not just syntax.
What would change with unequal inclusion probabilities? What if effort were
zero, units differed across cruises, or a join duplicated tow records?
:::

## Exercise solution

```{r}
#| label: exercise-solution
answer <- tbl(con, "survey") |>
  filter(year == 2024L, species == "pollock") |>
  mutate(cpue = catch_kg / effort_km2) |>
  group_by(stratum) |>
  summarise(mean_cpue = mean(cpue, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_observed = sum(as.integer(!is.na(cpue)), na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(stratum) |>
  collect()
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(answer$mean_cpue, c(24, 11))))
knitr::kable(answer, digits = 2)
```

The shelf ratio of sums is `154 / 6 = 25.67`, not 24.
Choose the estimator based on the sampling design and analysis question.

## Take this workflow to your next paper

1. Validate a typed extract from the authoritative source.
2. Publish an approved, immutable Parquet snapshot with a dictionary.
3. Query lazily with DuckDB; collect only what the analysis needs.
4. Test sample sizes, keys, units, missingness, and known results.
5. Render tables/figures from code and archive input + software provenance.

**Start small:** replace one repeated CSV scan, compare results, then scale.

## Render environment

```{r}
#| label: environment
#| echo: false
packages <- c("duckdb", "DBI", "dplyr", "dbplyr", "knitr", "rmarkdown")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Software = c("R", packages),
  Version = c(as.character(getRversion()),
              vapply(packages, function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p)), ""))
))
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```

These are the versions used for **this render**, not a substitute for a reviewed
project lockfile. Full R session details are saved in `_demo/session-info.txt`.
